title: EPIDERMOLYSIS BULLOSA SIMPLEX 7, WITH NEPHROPATHY AND DEAFNESS

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that epidermolysis bullosa simplex-7 with nephropathy and deafness (EBS7) is caused by homozygous mutation in the CD151 gene on chromosome 11p15.5.

checks.claim: Epidermolysis bullosa simplex-7 with nephropathy and deafness (EBS7) is caused by homozygous mutation in the CD151 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: The 3 patients are homozygous for a single nucleotide insertion (G383) in exon 5 of CD151, causing a frameshift and premature stop signal at codon 140.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports a homozygous CD151 mutation in patients with nephritis, and the sibs also had deafness and pretibial EB. The EBS7 disease name is not in the paper, and the third patient's features are not given.

checks.claim: The CD151 gene is located on chromosome 11p15.5.
checks.evidence_quote: It is encoded by a gene at the same position on chromosome 11p15.5 as the MER2 blood group gene.
checks.explanation: The abstract places the gene at 11p15.5.

paragraphs.text: Epidermolysis bullosa simplex-7 with nephropathy and deafness (EBS7) is a disorder in which pretibial epidermolysis bullosa occurs together with hereditary nephritis that progresses to end-stage renal disease, and with sensorineural deafness. Reported patients also had nail dystrophy and lacrimal duct stenosis (Kagan et al., 1988; Karamatic Crew et al., 2004).

checks.explanation: The sibs had pretibial EB together with hereditary nephritis.

paragraphs.text: Kagan et al. (1988) described 2 sibs from an Oriental Jewish family with hereditary nephritis, pretibial epidermolysis bullosa, and beta-thalassemia minor. Both sibs had proteinuria in the nephrotic range and developed end-stage renal disease. They needed dialysis (hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis) from the ages of 14 and 16 years, respectively. They also had nasolacrimal duct stenosis, nail dystrophy, and sensorineural hearing loss.

paragraphs.text: Karamatic Crew et al. (2004) studied 3 patients of Indian Jewish origin with end-stage kidney disease, 2 of whom were sibs. As well as hereditary nephritis, the sibs had sensorineural deafness, pretibial epidermolysis bullosa, and beta-thalassemia minor. The patients also had pretibial bullous skin lesions. The red blood cells of all 3 patients were negative for the MER2 blood group antigen.

paragraphs.text: Karamatic Crew et al. (2004) studied 3 MER2-negative patients of Indian Jewish origin with end-stage kidney disease, 2 of whom were sibs. They examined CD151, the gene that lies at the same position on chromosome 11p15.5 as the MER2 blood group gene. All 3 patients were homozygous for a single-nucleotide insertion (G383) in exon 5 of CD151, which caused a frameshift and a premature stop signal at codon 140. The resulting truncated protein would lack the integrin-binding domain. The authors showed that CD151 carries the MER2 blood group antigen and is present on erythrocytes. CD151 forms laminin-binding complexes with integrins alpha-3/beta-1 and alpha-6/beta-1 in kidney and with alpha-3/beta-1 and alpha-6/beta-4 in skin. The authors concluded that CD151 is essential for the proper assembly of the glomerular and tubular basement membranes in the kidney, has functional significance in the skin, and is probably a component of the inner ear.

paragraphs.text: Karamatic Crew et al. (2004) studied 3 MER2-negative patients of Indian Jewish origin with end-stage kidney disease, including 2 sibs who also had sensorineural deafness, pretibial epidermolysis bullosa, and beta-thalassemia minor. All 3 were homozygous for a 1-bp insertion of G at nucleotide 383 (383_384insG) in exon 5 of the CD151 gene. The insertion caused a frameshift and a premature stop signal at codon 140, which would produce a truncated protein lacking the integrin-binding domain. The patients' red blood cells did not express the MER2 blood group antigen, which is carried on CD151.
